definitions.explanation: An imaginary line running from the North Pole to the South Pole on a globe or map, used to measure longitude. The prime meridian (0 degrees) passes through Greenwich, England.

examples.japanese: {経線|けいせん}は{南北|なんぼく}に{走|はし}る。
examples.english: Meridians run from north to south.

examples.japanese: {地図|ちず}には{経線|けいせん}と{緯線|いせん}が{描|えが}かれている。
examples.english: Meridians and parallels are drawn on the map.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{標準時|ひょうじゅんじ}は{東経|とうけい}135{度|ど}の{経線|けいせん}を{基準|きじゅん}にしている。
examples.english: Japan Standard Time is based on the meridian at 135 degrees east longitude.

notes:
Composed of {経|けい} (longitude; passing through) and {線|せん} (line). A fundamental geography term taught in schools. Always used in contrast with {緯線|いせん} (parallel, line of latitude), and the pair is essential for understanding maps and global coordinates.

Note the homophone {罫線|けいせん} (ruled line), which has the same reading but a completely different meaning.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {経線|けいせん}と{緯線|いせん}: meridians and parallels
- {本初|ほんしょ}{子午線|しごせん}: prime meridian (0 degrees)
- {東経|とうけい}…{度|ど}の{経線|けいせん}: the meridian at … degrees east longitude
- {日付変更線|ひづけへんこうせん}: International Date Line

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {緯線|いせん}: parallel, line of latitude — runs east-west; the counterpart to {経線|けいせん}
- {子午線|しごせん}: meridian — a more formal or literary synonym
- {経度|けいど}: longitude — the numerical measurement, not the line itself
